title: Controlled Company, Controlled Story
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: Founder voting or board control can shape who appoints leaders and approves major corporate acts, but it cannot guarantee truthful archives, good design, worker voice, or permanent cultural legitimacy.
One frame holds a named designer, a model, a photographer, a collection, and an institutional record—separate roles that public shorthand often compresses.
narrativeSequence.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · VOTE — What does the vote actually reach?. Record security class, votes per share, ownership date, agreements, transfer limits, quorum, reserved matters, and the exact filing. Do not convert disclosed voting power into a claim about every creative decision.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · BOARD — Who directs the corporation?. For a Delaware corporation, inspect certificate, bylaws, board composition, committee and delegation records with §141. Founder status alone is not a board rule.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · STORY — Which systems shape public memory?. Map archive access, approval language, publicity, account control, historian or curator independence, contributor correction, and disputed records separately from corporate votes.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · CONSTRAINT — Who can challenge the controller?. Identify independent directors, contractual rights, worker and collaborator channels, law, fiduciary review, press scrutiny, archive policy, and correction routes without assuming any is effective in a particular company.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
